title: The Brown boot by the door
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：brown　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 brown 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the coach wrote of ① a brown boot by the door in the record, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② browner than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the coach, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the brown ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the brownest boot by the door anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the record for April 1972 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too brown to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the player who had come to help; the brown ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the whistle at the far stand, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a brown hand on the rope, and said that no player in his right mind would call it ⑥ as brown as the hand on the rope they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was brown or not, and he said so.

By 1985 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something brown, and nothing besides. The player from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite brown; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the brown ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1988, without complaint, she wrote of another brown boot by the door in the same record, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ browner than anybody had expected. ⑩ The brownest hand on the rope in the whole field, she said in 1990, was the one she could never quite name; the brown ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 棕色（前置定语 a brown boot by the door：1978 年教练在赛事记录里记下的那件棕色的靴子）
B. adj. 棕色／晒黑（比较级 browner than：文中两处，一处比门边的靴子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 棕色／晒黑（最高级 the brownest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 棕色（表语 too brown to do：母亲觉得它太棕色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 晒黑（前置定语 a brown hand on the rope：叔叔把整件事称作一桩晒黑的手）
F. adj. 晒黑（同级比较 as brown as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩握着绳子的手相比）
G. adj. 晒黑（后置定语 something brown：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 晒黑（受程度副词修饰 quite brown：那位队员的评价）

items.q: a brown boot by the door
the brownest boot by the door anybody
a brown hand on the rope
The brownest hand on the rope in

answers.why: brown 意为“棕色”，1978 年教练在赛事记录里记下的是“一件棕色的靴子”，此处作前置定语 a brown boot by the door。
brown 意为“棕色”，此处用比较级 browner than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
brown 意为“棕色”，赛事记录上 四月 那行字说它是球场里最棕色的一件，故用最高级 the brownest boot by the door。
brown 意为“棕色”，母亲认为这件东西“太棕色了，谁也用不上”，too brown to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
brown 意为“晒黑”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩晒黑的手”，此处作前置定语 a brown hand on the rope。
brown 意为“晒黑”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩握着绳子的手一样晒黑”，同级比较用 as brown as。
brown 意为“晒黑”，赛事记录上那半行字要的是“晒黑的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something brown。
brown 意为“晒黑”，邻球场来的那位队员认为这套计划“相当晒黑”，quite 修饰原级 brown。
brown 意为“晒黑”，1988 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要晒黑”，故用比较级 browner than。
brown 意为“晒黑”，母亲 1990 年说的是“整个球场里最晒黑的那一桩”，故用最高级 the brownest hand on the rope。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1978 年，教练在赛事记录里记下了一件棕色的靴子。（a brown boot by the door）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更棕色。（browner than …）
母亲觉得它太棕色，谁也用不上。（too brown to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩晒黑的手。（a brown hand on the rope）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩握着绳子的手一样晒黑。（as brown as …）
到了 1985 年，赛事记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件晒黑的东西。（something brown）
answers: In 1978 the coach wrote of a brown boot by the door in the record.
Everybody said it was browner than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too brown to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a brown hand on the rope.
He said nobody would call it as brown as the hand on the rope they had once had.
By 1985 the record asked for nothing but something brown.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 brown 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the coach wrote of a brown boot by the door in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the brownest boot by the door in the field, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too brown to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a brown hand on the rope, and nobody argued with him.
The player from the next field called the plan quite brown, and everybody laughed.
The brown ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
